title: Magnetic Stabilization of the Greenhill Instability and Hysteretic Switching in Slender Rods
summary: In a bulk ferromagnet, magnetic energy is six orders of magnitude weaker than elastic energy. Slenderness removes this disparity. In a thin ferromagnetic rod, the two energies scale differently with aspect ratio, and an ordinary nickel wire deforms nonlinearly even under modest remote fields. We develop a three-dimensional variational theory of a ferromagnetic Kirchhoff rod under gravity and magnetic loading and study it through bifurcation analysis, computation, and experiment.
